Proposed mainboard migration and a PPP bid are not completed listings or awarded projects.

sections.title: 1. Executive Verdict
sections.text: Asarfi has a plausible regional hospital-growth story, but it is not yet a proven cash compounder. Installed oncology and super-specialty capacity are producing strong revenue growth; the corresponding payer receivables, debt and land commitments must also be funded. At the secondary October 19 close₹188.50, the funded existing-capacity base produces 5.69% over five years, below a 15% hurdle. BQS5.76, GQS6.75 and IAS3.84 support a conditional watchlist rather than a favorable entry. All four gates are Conditional. No proposed migration, bid or credit upgrade is treated as equity value by itself. [S1,S3,S8,M1]

sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: The legal/security identity is Asarfi Hospital Limited, ISIN INE0DN001027, BSE543943, with 19,677,300 issued shares verified by the June registrar reconciliation and current master. Scope is consolidated hospital plus wholly owned Asarfi Educational Foundation, but the foundation’s₹0.1196 crore cash is not presumed distributable to public shareholders. Its separate statements use thousands, unlike the group’s lakhs; units are converted before consolidation comparisons. Cutoff is October 20,2026 and the price date October 19. FY26 signed accounts are the financial anchor; Q1FY27 is separately labeled. The primary shareholding record says SME, and the AGM notice proposes BSE-mainboard/NSE migration. An AGM index reports shareholder action, but no effective migration notice was verified; a decoded master listing date does not prove migration. [S1,S6,S9,S10,M1]

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: Scores reuse GOV5, MOAT6, REV8, DUR6, CAP6, CASH4, BAL5, EXEC6, EARN7, R2, D3, P4 and L7. BQS is 5.76, GQS6.75, IAS3.84; no cap or reweighting is applied. REV is capped at 8 because a short ramp-up history and Medium persistence confidence do not justify 9–10. R follows funded 5.69%, not a positive terminal value from a cash-deficit path. Coarse liquidity starts at 9 and is reduced to 7 for secondary proxy, lot and execution uncertainty. The₹5 lakh position is illustrative, not a recommended allocation. [E1–E8]

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text: The group operates a Dhanbad super-specialty hospital and dedicated cancer facility, with educational activities a small adjunct. Inpatient treatments, outpatient visits, diagnostics, pharmacy and support services have different revenue and cash cycles. Cash patients, insurers and institutional/government payers must not be treated as equally liquid billings. Beds create value only when appropriately staffed, utilized and paid for; specialist availability, referral trust and clinical reputation are operational constraints, not just construction costs. Local scale and existing infrastructure reduce the need to construct a wholly new hospital for each increment of occupancy. The foundation is not separately valued as a freely distributable cash business, and intercompany advances are not added to consolidated equity twice. [S1,S3]

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: The regional catchment and oncology offering support MOAT6 rather than a national-platform premium. Clinical teams, referral relationships, equipment and service breadth can be difficult to replicate quickly, but concentration in one geography and dependence on clinicians and reimbursement rules limit pricing independence. Q1 cancer revenue was₹9.8 crore versus₹37.1 crore for the super-specialty unit, and the largest specialties are meaningful contributors. These are issuer disclosures, not verified market shares. National hospital multiples are not directly comparable to this single-market SME, its payer mix or capital structure. Exit EBIT8×/12×/16× is an analyst sensitivity range, not a claimed peer median or migration-driven rerating forecast. [S1,S3]

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Consolidated revenue was₹70.7033/84.4004/121.7776/173.5029 crore for FY23–26, with latest 42.48% growth and an indicative three-year CAGR~34.9%. Earlier years retain their original presentation: the latest FY25 comparative moved₹1.2118 crore from other income into operating revenue. PAT was₹8.0153/4.1616/10.5762/16.6609 crore; the FY24 decline shows why a rebound is not a straight-line long-cycle trend. Q1FY27 revenue₹47.53 crore grew 33.2%, EBITDA₹9.46 crore 35.3% and PAT₹4.27 crore 36.7%. The presentation’s₹6.88 crore EBIT includes₹0.57 crore other income; operating EBIT used here is₹6.31 crore. Do not capitalize deposit interest or rents at the hospital multiple. [S1,S3,S4,S5]

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Q1 disclosed 285 super-specialty beds at 59% occupancy and 65 cancer beds at 56%, versus 250/65 beds and 64%/42% occupancy a year earlier. ARPOB was₹23,498/₹31,892. More beds and improved oncology occupancy explain part of growth; lower super-specialty occupancy on expanded capacity cautions against calling every bed equally productive. A raw occupied-bed calculation exceeds disclosed inpatient revenue, so the model calibrates by 0.84588, explicitly not an asserted count of effective beds. FY25–26 incremental NOPAT/capital is about 49.0%, while FY26 NOPAT/average capital is only 12.0%. The gap is consistent with installed-capacity ramp and timing, not proof of perpetually exceptional project returns. The June 27 board approved a PPP medical-college bid and refundable₹3.52 crore security, potentially through a guarantee or insurance bond, explicitly not an award. No associated project revenue or capital is put in the ordinary case. IPO-use tables show all four original allocations utilized; no new free IPO pot is invented. [S1,S3,S7,S8]

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: The FY26 auditor reports accounting-software audit trails enabled from April 16,2025 and Hospital Information System trails from February 24,2026, while HRMS lacked the feature. No tampering was identified in the auditor’s test checks. Bank current-asset statements did not agree with the books; management explains that only corporate debtors were reported to banks. This is a disclosed control/reporting gap requiring remediation, not evidence that revenue, cash or patient records were fabricated. The FY24 audit-qualification annexure also concerned the audit-trail feature and did not quantify a change to the financial figures. Related-party disclosed items include remuneration, professional fees, lab services, royalty and CSR to a trust influenced by the CFO. They require commercial and collection scrutiny but are not automatically diversion. The parent advanced₹0.9058 crore to its education subsidiary duringFY26, reaching₹1.7681 crore; it is eliminated in consolidation and cannot be added as a second asset. CRISIL’s October 7 upgrade to BBB/Stable is a lender-risk opinion, not an equity recommendation; it also notes earlier CARE noncooperation. The issuer’s reporting and improved controls are offsets, not proof that all remediation is complete. [S1,S2,S5]

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text: The FY26 maturity table totals ₹47.0474 crore of term-loan payments, versus ₹43.5878 crore booked noncurrent plus current term principal. Its first-year figure ₹8.4386 crore also differs from ₹8.5790 crore in the current-debt note. The difference may involve interest, timing or presentation; a complete reconciliation was not found. The model uses booked principal for amortization and separately reserves ₹3.4596 crore, with an early-payment sensitivity. This is a conservative research reserve, not a finding of unrecorded borrowing. Consolidated FY25/FY26 CFO is−₹4.3439/+₹18.3043 crore, a ratio of sums to PAT of 0.513. Three-year conversion rises to 1.275 because FY24 included₹19.8692 crore supplier inflow during construction. FY26 CFO less cash capex is only₹0.1950 crore, and after₹4.2437 crore financing interest it is−₹4.0487 crore. AS3 classification puts interest in financing; it is not absent from total cash. Receivables rose to₹54.1215 crore, while audited amounts older than six months fell from₹9.1685 to₹2.2907 crore. The rating’s age-direction text is inconsistent with its own figures; the audited ageing controls here. Rating PAT₹17.08/₹10.98 crore aligns with parent₹17.0766/₹10.9797 crore, not consolidated PAT. Its operating-income definition remains different and is not spliced in. Liens are stated on₹3.864 crore short and₹4.864 crore long deposits; the repeated₹3.864 crore description may overlap, so both are conservatively restricted. The₹0.304 crore LIC account is not credited against gross actuarial obligations without a reconciliation. [S1,S2,S4]

sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: The model starts with actual March 31 balances and 67 monthly dates through October 2031. Q1 revenue/operating earnings calibrate the initial quarter; monthly cash and the rest of the seven-month entry stub remain estimates. Base terminal occupancy is 72%/70%, annual ARPOB growth 5%, OPD growth 7%, normalized EBIT margin 13.5% and exit multiple 12×. No extra beds are assumed. Maintenance is 1.1×D&A, plus equipment capital on growth beyond the installed Q1 run rate and₹2 crore first-year completion cash; opening CWIP/capital advances convert once without a second cash payment. Base terminal revenue is₹298.30 crore, equity price₹248.55, and IRR5.69%. Bull 82%/82% occupancy,7% ARPOB growth,16% margin and 16× EBIT yields₹497.87 and 21.44%. Ordinary bear 50%/45% occupancy,3% ARPOB growth,10% margin,8× exit and 2 points higher WC intensity has an estimated September cash gap₹0.6009 crore; its positive terminal calculation is not an investor return. If genuinely free short deposits are accessible by month 6 instead of 12, the funded bear return is−16.86%, a conditional sensitivity. Base 15%-hurdle entry is₹123.57, or exit EBIT must be 18.38× with all other inputs unchanged. Current tax, capital creditors, employee claims, land dues and debt are funded/retained once. [S1,S3,M1]

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Restrained survival combines 15% lower revenue, no ARPOB/OPD growth,11% EBIT margin,25% loss of audited older receivables,₹1 crore additional collection delay, full contingent-payment provision and early legacy benefits. It remains funded without new debt/equity, minimum cash₹4.3773 crore. Lower volume releases some WC, so this is distinct from a growing but slow-collecting bear case. Existing drawn working-capital debt₹13.9695 crore is assumed to remain available, with interest and terminal repayment; no new limit is invented. Nonrenewal at month 12, accelerated land payment, early payment of the maturity-table difference, full₹3.52 crore bid cash collateral or₹5 crore extra collection delay can exhaust cash. The extreme stacked boundary fails in its estimated April stub and is not evidence of an actual default. A separate 100-bed/₹50 crore expansion and rescue case includes interest, capped new credit,3% equity fees and half-price dilution; it is neither awarded nor available financing. [S1,S8]

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: A fivefold or tenfold per-share value in five years needs roughly 37.97% or 58.49% annual compounding without a dividend/rerating contribution. The base existing-capacity terminal revenue₹298.30 crore implies a much smaller path than that; even the bull terminal share value₹497.87 is about 2.64× the quote. Faster occupancy cannot exceed physical/staffed capacity indefinitely, ARPOB increases can affect access and demand, and new beds require capital before cash returns. Mainboard migration may change trading access but does not itself add operating earnings. A tenbagger thesis would require substantially stronger, funded and cash-realized execution than the ordinary analysis establishes. [S1,S3,S8]

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Priority checks are payer-specific collections and ageing; actual free-deposit maturity/liens; bank renewal/covenants; the maturity-to-principal bridge; current JIADA payment terms; and whether the approved bid security was issued, collateralized or released. Recheck occupancy on the effective-bed definition and reconcile it to inpatient revenue instead of extrapolating headline capacity. Obtain proof of full accounting/HIS/HRMS audit trails, bank-return reconciliation and completed charge registration. Track actual clinician retention, cash operating earnings and capex needed for incremental utilization. Verify effective exchange admission and lot changes only from dated exchange notices, not a shareholder vote. These are research triggers, not a promise of automatic monitoring. [S1,S3,S6,S8,S10]

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: The company reclassified ₹7.1385 crore JIADA land dues as noncurrent. It reports that a March 7,2025 High Court order removed the company and JIADA from the described proceedings and that the plaintiffs undertook not to execute a decree against its allotted 11.92 acres, while leaving separate proceedings possible. Management also seeks revised cost/payment terms. Those disclosures do not extinguish the recorded payable or prove all title/payment questions resolved; the model settles it explicitly rather than treating reclassification as free cash. The annual report identifies four consumer compensation cases in which the hospital is a party, aggregating ₹1.1113 crore, and ₹0.9577 crore corporate tie-up bank guarantees. These are disclosed contingent claims, not findings of medical negligence, actual payment orders or invoked guarantees. The model pays half over the second year and retains the rest at exit, with a full-payment sensitivity; it does not assign liability to individual clinicians or disclose patient information. The final classification is a conditional watchlist with an unattractive base return at the reference price. Regional execution has improved, and restrained survival is credible, but cash timing and current working-capital facilities matter. A rating/annual difference is not automatically a reliability failure: this review resolves the PAT scope issue and preserves remaining revenue definitions, while using conservative claim reserves. Upgrade needs sustained collected earnings, adequate renewal/funding evidence, completed control remediation and a price that clears the return hurdle without speculative expansion or rerating. [S1,S2,S3]

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: The source ledger distinguishes audited annual amounts, company operating metrics, rating opinion, secondary market data, calculations and scenario assumptions. All major opening current tax, employee, supplier, capital, debt, land and contingent claims receive exactly one base treatment; assets are not recovered through WC and also added as terminal cash. Deposits pledged to lenders are not treated as free operating funding, and foundation units/cash are kept separate. The IPO table’s stale period label and all unverified effective listings, guarantee issuance and debt/lien reconciliations remain visible. Exact quoted security prices are dated observations, not trading advice or guaranteed execution. Scores are framework heuristics, not calibrated return predictors. [S1–S10,M1,M_SECURITY_SPEC]

valuation.type: Funded existing-capacity common-equity model; unfunded bear has no IRR
valuation.units: INR crore; shares crore; price INR
valuation.method: 67 dated monthly rows: Q1FY27 revenue/EBIT calibration, estimated cash bridge through October entry, then five years. Occupied-bed/ARPOB cohorts calibrated to actual Q1 inpatient revenue; the calibration factor is not an asserted count of effective beds. No unannounced capacity in ordinary cases. OPD/other revenue modeled separately. Margins exclude other income; no future interest/rent assumed. Maintenance 1.1 x depreciation, incremental equipment capital above the already-installed Q1 run rate at 5 x additional revenue/capital and 2 crore minimum first-year completion cash; opening CWIP/capital advances commission once noncash. Book term/current debt paid using disclosed maturity buckets but reconciled to booked principal; unexplained 3.4596 crore difference retained separately, early-payment sensitivity. Existing working-capital debt held at current drawn amount with interest and terminal repayment; no uncommitted increment or automatic rescue. Nonrenewal stress separate. Current tax, benefits, capital creditors, JIADA land and contingent claims paid once; unpaid claims retained at exit. Gratuity LIC account excluded unless dated recovery sensitivity; gross employee obligations retained. DTL reserved conservatively at exit with no projected release. Free short/long FDs release month 12/24; separately disclosed liens on both maturities conservatively treated as distinct and carried at facevalue against terminal claims, never operating funding. Foundation cash excluded from free corporate cash; intercompany loan not added as a consolidated asset. June 27 approved 3.52 crore bid security is not established as issued, cash collateral posted, or a project award. No ordinary project income/capex assumed; full cash-collateral posting and 180 day refund tested separately. Unfunded branches receive no investorIRR.

GOV.reason: Control gaps persist across years but auditors identified no tampering; related relationships and public disclosure are bounded. Specific remediation, bank reconciliation and charge completion remain necessary; no severe override from a process finding alone.

MOAT.reason: Regional installed clinical infrastructure and oncology specialization offer catchment advantages, but doctor dependence, local concentration and payer bargaining limit durable pricing evidence.

REV.reason: Four-year indicative growth is strong and latest comparable annual growth 42.48%; installed-capacity ramp and reclassification mean no full-cycle 9–10 claim. Medium-confidence persistence caps at 8.

DUR.reason: Existing 285+65 beds have utilization headroom and improving cancer occupancy. Growth requires staff, patient demand and collections; an unawarded PPP bid adds no certain runway value.

CAP.reason: Incremental capacity-ramp return is strong but mature average return about 12% is only around the 12–16% assumed capital-cost range. High historical construction spend and claim timing prevent extrapolating one-year incremental returns.

CASH.reason: Two-year CFO/PAT0.513 before financing interest, despite three-year 1.275 buoyed by construction-period supplier credit. Receivables improved in ageing but rose in amount, and after capex/interest cash remains weak. Not enough persistent<=3 evidence for a mechanical GQS cap.

BAL.reason: Base and restrained stress are funded at current drawn facilities, but deposit liens, land claims and demand debt create sensitivity to timing and renewal. Optional expansion is not mistaken for a current solvency failure.

EXEC.reason: Strong annual/Q1 growth and cancer occupancy improve utilization of existing assets; slower super-specialty occupancy and control follow-through temper the record.

EARN.reason: Operating EBIT nearly doubled and Q1 underlying EBIT grew; FY25 liability write-off and nonoperating income are removed from the forecast. Four-year earnings include a FY24 dip and do not establish long-cycle persistence.

R.reason: Funded base 5.69% falls in the 5–8% band at a 15% hurdle. No IRR is assigned to the unfunded ordinary bear path.

D.reason: A modest adverse WC/margin combination has a funding gap; even conditional earlier-FD-access bear returns−16.86%. Restrained lower-volume survival is a real offset, not proof of downside protection.

P.reason: Existing utilization improvement has support, but institutional-payer collection, clinician costs, control quality and narrow cash headroom make a high-return outcome uncertain at the quote.

L.reason: The 1.16 day proxy starts at 9; downgrade 2 points for secondary turnover estimation,₹188,500 lot granularity and unavailable current depth/restrictions. All 60 observations exist.
